import random, itertools
n_points=11
point_degrees=[3]*n_points
block_sizes=[4,4,4]+[3]*7
# backtracking
pairs=set()
blocks=[]
rem=point_degrees[:]
# generate possible blocks sorted maybe dynamic

def search(i):
    if i==len(block_sizes):
        return all(r==0 for r in rem)
    s=block_sizes[i]
    # choose points with rem >0; enforce nondecreasing maybe break symmetry for first block
    candidates=[p for p in range(n_points) if rem[p]>0]
    # sort combos maybe weighted
    combos=[]
    for comb in itertools.combinations(candidates,s):
        if any(tuple(sorted((a,b))) in pairs for a,b in itertools.combinations(comb,2)):
            continue
        # feasibility: rem not too high for remaining blocks? simple
        combos.append(comb)
    random.shuffle(combos)
    # heuristic prefer high rem
    combos.sort(key=lambda c: -sum(rem[p] for p in c)+random.random()*0.01)
    for comb in combos:
        for p in comb: rem[p]-=1
        newpairs=[tuple(sorted((a,b))) for a,b in itertools.combinations(comb,2)]
        for pr in newpairs: pairs.add(pr)
        blocks.append(comb)
        # pruning: total rem equals remaining sizes
        ok=True
        if sum(rem)!=sum(block_sizes[i+1:]): ok=False
        # each rem <= remaining blocks count
        if ok and any(r<0 or r>len(block_sizes)-i-1 for r in rem): ok=False
        # pair availability for each point enough? each future incidence with point needs distinct co-points no repeated pairs. point p has 10-(used partners) available partners.
        # approximate max future blocks point p <= available partners // (min block size-1)
        if ok:
            for p in range(n_points):
                usedpartners=sum(1 for q in range(n_points) if q!=p and tuple(sorted((p,q))) in pairs)
                # need rem[p] future blocks, each uses at least 2 new partners if size3, maybe 3 if size4
                if rem[p]*2 > (n_points-1-usedpartners):
                    ok=False; break
        if ok:
            res=search(i+1)
            if res: return res
        blocks.pop()
        for pr in newpairs: pairs.remove(pr)
        for p in comb: rem[p]+=1
    return None

# no triangles
